title: I had Claude Opus 5.5 one-shot a 3Blue1Brown-style video on how I balance my game with reinforcement learning
author: bestof-games
selftext:
I'm making a small autobattler for iPhone (Beaver Keep, Godot) and use a PPO agent to find balance problems: cards that dominate, cards nobody picks, seeds you can't win. I asked Opus 5.5 to explain the setup in the style of 3Blue1Brown, and this is what it made in one go, including the training run, the animations and the replays of the agent playing. I would like to add a voiceover, what do you think? 

What do you use to balance your game? RL, scripted bots, spreadsheets, just playtesting?  
How do you approach level generation?

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body:
Does the agent actually play the game as is?

Do you have a headless mode or something similar?

replies.author: bestof-games
replies.body:
I wouldn’t say RL agent plays the game “as is”. I ported the game logic 1:1 to python for faster simulation. The agent doesn’t “see” the screen, it uses the game state as input. 

Yes, it runs in headless python mode. It’s much faster than running it in godot, no need to render anything.

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body: Ah, so you made a second version of the game. I was wondering for my game how to automate playing. Perhaps a simple headless version with extra input for controls and output to read the game state might be enough. Then have some cheap model play the game, at best a dozen of them in parallel.

replies.author: bestof-games
replies.body: Important differentiation.I did not use an LLM or JEV to play my game. I trained my own specialized machine learning model from scratch. No transformer, no language model.  Just a neural networks.

replies.author: bestof-games
replies.body: But technically the agents plays the game as is. It’s just not using the UI directly. I just decides which move to make based on the game state.
